## 14. Local execution

**`millwright run <wf>` is always local; `millwright dispatch <wf>` is always cloud** —
the verb split makes running in the wrong place impossible. Reference session:
`prototypes/local-runner/SESSION.md`.

Shared core, two thin hosts: the pure decider library + step shim run in-process
against two seams — **`Executor`** (`StartBuild` ↔ `docker run`) and **`StateSink`**
(DynamoDB ↔ `.millwright/runs/local-N.json`). Same DAG logic, SKIPPED semantics,
terminal states; Ctrl-C sets the same `cancelRequested` flag through the same path.

The parity contract:

| | Cloud run | Local run | Parity |
|---|---|---|---|
| Definition + synth | synth at triggering commit (CodeBuild, `npm ci`) | same code, in-process bundle (sub-second; node_modules fidelity gap accepted) | **same model** |
| Job order / retries / skips | decider Lambda | same decider, in-process | **same code** |
| Step status + SKIPPED | shim → DynamoDB | same shim → local state file | **same code** |
| Job environment | CodeBuild + declared image | local docker, same image (host-native arch; `--platform` for exact) | **same image** |
| Image pull/auth | CodeBuild role / synthesized ECR grants | user's own docker config — millwright does no registry auth | delegated |
| Source | clean checkout at commit | git-aware **working-tree copy** per job (no bind mount); `--clean` = `git archive HEAD` | ≈, explicit |
| Secrets | SSM/SM → env vars | gitignored `.millwright/secrets.env` (or `--secrets-file`) → env vars; missing declared secrets fail before any job starts | same contract |
| Artifacts | S3 run prefix | `.millwright/runs/<id>/<job>/<name>` | same layout |
| Dependency cache | S3 keyed | local dir, same keys | same semantics |
| IAM / AWS calls | per-job least privilege | **zero AWS calls** | absent, by design |
| Compute sizing | honored | ignored (noted); `timeout` enforced | advisory |
| Run identity | `ci#142`, in `runs list` | `local-N` per clone under gitignored `.millwright/`, never in `runs list` | separate namespaces |

Inner loop: `--job X` runs one job, satisfying `consumes` from the most recent local
run's artifacts (reuse printed with age; error names the producing job if absent);
`--with-deps` runs the ancestor subgraph. Trigger predicates are never evaluated
locally; `MILLWRIGHT_*` context vars are synthesized from the checkout (dirty tree →
`-dirty` sha), with overrides like `--as-tag v9.9.9-test`. Typed inputs prompt
interactively or come from `--input k=v`. Privileged jobs mount the host docker socket
with a one-line fidelity warning. Concurrency config is carried but not enforced.

---

## 15. CLI command surface

Flags shown are the v1 contract; `--deployment` / `MILLWRIGHT_DEPLOYMENT` applies
everywhere (§3.4). Exit codes are scriptable: `logs -f` mirrors the run result.

```
Setup & ops
  millwright init                          scaffold the thin CDK app
  millwright setup [--pat]                 GitHub App manifest handshake (browser) | PAT mode
  millwright repo add <owner/repo> [--secrets-refs <refs>] [--no-pr-polling]
                                           write repo config, mint+install deploy key
  millwright repo update <owner/repo> [--secrets-refs <refs>] [--pr-polling <bool>]
  millwright repo list | repo remove <owner/repo>        ◊ (spec-filled, §18)
  millwright doctor                        verify chain: SSM manifest, App creds, deploy
                                           keys, poller ticking; report CodeBuild
                                           concurrency + IAM role quotas
  millwright refresh-host-keys             re-pin GitHub SSH host keys from /meta
  millwright secrets set <name> [--scope <scope>]        author a workflow secret

Definition
  millwright synth                         compile workflows.ts, print model/lint results

Execution
  millwright run <wf> [--job X [--with-deps]] [--clean] [--platform <p>]
                 [--secrets-file <path>] [--input k=v ...] [--as-tag <tag>]
                 [--parallel N]            always local
  millwright dispatch <wf> [--ref <ref>] [--input k=v ...]   always cloud

Observability
  millwright logs [-f] [<run>] [--job <name>] [--failed] [--full]
                                           no-arg -f waits for the next run to appear
                                           (push-and-watch: git push && millwright logs -f)
  millwright runs list [--workflow <wf>] [--ref <ref>] [--status <s>]   ~20/page
  millwright runs show [<run>]             DAG + per-job/per-step status, culprit inline
  millwright runs rerun <run> [--failed]
  millwright runs cancel <run>
```

- **Run identity**: workflow-scoped run numbers (`ci#142`); an internal unique id
  exists but is never required typing. Latest-run defaults: `logs -f` and `runs show`
  with no run argument resolve to the most recent run (scoped by `--workflow`).
- **No web UI in v1.** GitHub check runs are team-glance visibility; the CLI needs no
  auth story beyond AWS credentials and keeps working during GitHub outages. Raw
  CloudWatch stays an escape hatch via deep links, never the UX.
- `logs -f` implementation: **polled `GetLogEvents` (~2 s), not CloudWatch Live Tail**
  ($0.01/min sessions and session limits buy latency CI logs don't need); run-level
  interleaved tail, docker-compose style, job-name prefixes + lifecycle markers.
- Retention: run metadata 90 d, logs 30 d (deployment knobs). No log archival.

**Setup flow** (discrete guided commands, no wizard):
`init` → plain `cdk deploy` (never wrapped — the operator owns the infra artifact) →
`setup` → `repo add` per repo → `doctor`.

---

## 16. Latency and cost expectations

| | Figure | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Push → detection | ~30–90 s typical, ~2 min worst | ticket 002 |
| CodeBuild PROVISIONING | 2–7 s across the whole v1 matrix | ticket 012, measured |
| Push → first log line | **"typically under two minutes"** — promise without hedging | ticket 012 |
| Polling stack | ~$0.80–2.40/mo at 10–50 repos | ticket 002 |
| CMK | ~$1/mo (the one standing cost) | ticket 008 |
| Compute at 100 runs/day × 5 min | ~$51/mo on arm1.small ($10–$204 across 50×2 min → 200×10 min) | ticket 001 |
| Per-build minute rounding | +5–15% at typical job lengths | ticket 001 |
| Concurrent-start bursts | intermittent 30–40 s QUEUED on fresh accounts; queue, don't fail | ticket 012 |

---

## 17. Amendments log — contradictions resolved (later decision wins)

1. **Tier-1 polling transport/credential**: 002 designed HTTPS + App installation
   token → **011: SSH + deploy keys, always** (App tokens die ≤1 h into an API
   outage). 016 proved the SSH path live. The pkt-line/`ls-refs` parser carries over.
2. **System-credential storage**: 003 put App PEM + deploy keys in Secrets Manager →
   **011: SSM SecureString under the CMK** (SM would cost $0.40/secret/mo — 10x the
   polling stack at 50 repos; SSM standard tier is free and Ed25519 keys fit 4 KB).
3. **Deploy-key provisioning moment**: 011 said "at setup" → **014: at
   `millwright repo add`** (repos are dynamic, not deploy-time).
4. **Workflow-secret SSM path**: 008 decided `/millwright/secrets/<scope>/<NAME>` →
   folded under 014's deployment prefix as
   `/millwright/<name>/secrets/<scope>/<NAME>` for one coherent config plane. (Small;
   noted because it changes a decided literal path.)
5. **Launcher trigger-matching**: 004/006 never recorded how the launcher matches
   events → workflows pre-synth → **015: the synth-written per-ref registry** (§8.3),
   which also carries concurrency config.
6. **CodeBuild native S3 cache**: 001 suggested designing around it → **009: unused**
   (unkeyed per-project cache invites branch poisoning).
7. **Durable check queue**: 003 radiated "durable queue that flushes on recovery" →
   **010 satisfies it structurally** with desired-state reconciliation instead of a
   literal queue — strictly better (coalescing, no out-of-order).

None of these rise above "small": each was explicitly reconciled by a later ticket or
is a naming-level fold. **No unresolved contradictions remain.**

## 18. Gaps filled by this spec (not ticket-decided — review during build)

Marked ◊ throughout. In descending order of substance:

1. **Per-run job-role lifecycle** (§10.4) — creation point (decider, idempotent),
   naming, and sweep-based deletion are spec-authored. The only fill that warrants a
   real design pass (IAM quota pressure is real at ~500 roles/day).
2. **Cron firing mechanism** (§6.4) — poller tick evaluates cron from the
   default-branch registry entry. Natural (the tick and the registry both exist), but
   no ticket said it.
3. **Manual-dispatch transport** (§6.4) — CLI `PutEvents` under operator credentials,
   flowing the uniform launcher path.
4. Item/key naming for GROUP/REG/CHECK rows, SSM credential paths, S3 prefix names,
   `source.tar.gz` packaging, `repo list`/`repo remove` — pure naming/completeness
   fills.

## 19. Deferred (fog) and out of scope

**Deferred — may graduate later**: fail-fast (cancellation path now exists); GHA YAML
importer; notifications & badges; run web UI; `SecretFile` construct; `DockerCache`
construct; opportunistic webhook fast-path (would carry check re-run buttons);
check-run annotations; concurrency extensions (numeric limits, full FIFO, `reject`,
dispatch bypass).

**Out of scope — returns only if the destination is redrawn**: multi-tenancy /
millwright-as-a-service; code hosting and PR/review UX; webhook-*dependent* triggering;
soft-fail / allow-failure jobs.

nodes.title: v0.2.0
nodes.body:
# OntoBricks — Release Notes V0.2.0 **Release window:** May, 2026 **Test status:** all changes shipped with the suite green (≥ 1892 passing). --- ## Highlights - New end-to-end **Permissions model**: app-level perms come from Databricks, domain-level perms from the Teams matrix, with a 4-step refactor (declarative guards, body `data-*` attrs, CSS gating) and a hardened Viewer / read-only role across every ontology and mapping widget. - **Graph Chat** (formerly *Digital Twin*): natural-language chat with the knowledge graph, now session-aware and stable behind the deployed reverse proxy. - New in-app **Help Center** accessible from the navbar, including a Starter Guide, Workflow / FAQ accordions, a Data Access / GraphDB engine map (LadybugDB as default), and a refreshed About page. - **Lakebase registry backend** wired end-to-end. - **Databricks dev sandbox bundle** (`databricks.yml`): deploys **`ontobricks-020`** (main UI) and **`mcp-ontobricks`** (MCP); targets **`dev`** (Volume-only) and **`dev-lakebase`** (Volume + Lakebase Autoscaling `postgres` binding). Lakebase variables include **`lakebase_database_resource_segment`** (the `db-…` suffix from `databricks postgres list-databases … -o json`, not the Postgres `datname`) and **`lakebase_registry_schema`** (keep in sync with **`LAKEBASE_SCHEMA`** in `app.yaml`). - **Deploy & bootstrap scripts** aligned with the bundle: **`scripts/deploy.sh`** uses **`APP_NAME=ontobricks-020`**; **`make bootstrap-perms`** / **`make bootstrap-lakebase`** and the underlying shell scripts default to **`ontobricks-020`**, **`mcp-ontobricks`**, and the documented Lakebase project / schema-grant flow. - Major **domain-switching robustness** improvements (no more stale state, full-page loading overlay everywhere, including cross-domain bridges). - **Security**: patched two GitPython advisories (GHSA-rpm5-65cw-6hj4 and GHSA-x2qx-6953-8485 / CVE-2026-42284) by pinning `gitpython>=3.1.47` via uv constraint — transitive vuln only, no code-path exposure. --- ## Permissions & multi-tenant access control - App-level permissions now sourced from Databricks; domain-level permissions handled by the Teams matrix. - First-deploy bootstrap detects and fixes the app SP self-permission chicken-and-egg situation. - Viewer / read-only role: - Cascaded to all ontology and mapping widgets. - OWL preview no longer fails with "Unknown error" in read-only mode. - Belt-and-suspenders contextmenu blocker on design surfaces. - Gates data-source reset and all ontology / mapping imports. - Fixed Registry → Teams sub-menu leaking to non-admin users in the top navbar. - New three-level permission matrix tests + OWL endpoint contract tests. - 4-step permissions refactor: declarative guards, body `data-*` attributes, CSS-based gating. - Code-review fix-up: navbar role-badge inline CSS moved into `permissions.css`. ## Graph Chat (renamed from Digital Twin) - Natural-language chat over the knowledge graph. - Forwards `X-Forwarded-*` headers on loopback to fix a deployed 302 redirect issue. - All tools now use session-aware internal routes. - Code-review hardening pass: clean layering, consistent error handling, deduplication, class-first refactor. ## In-app Help Center - New navbar Help icon opens a modal with comprehensive documentation. - Refreshed About page to reflect the current product scope. - Visual pass: - Palette switched from blue to red/black (solid red, no gradients). - OntoBricks logo used in title and welcome hero. - Modal height locked (no resize when switching menu items). - Fixed double vertical scrollbar in tall sections (Starter Guide). - Removed horizontal scroll on the Welcome pipeline. - Removed grey borders on Workflow / FAQ accordions. - Starter Guide: - Added optional "Import Documents" step. - Rewrote the mapping step (manual or Auto-Map). - Added Data Access engine-map documentation, then generalized it to GraphDB (LadybugDB as default engine). ## Domain switching - Fixed stale session state leaking between domain switches — `DomainSession.import_from_file` now fully resets ontology, assignment, design layout, domain info, metadata, and triplestore before overlay. - Full-page "Loading {domain}…" overlay now appears for: - Graph switcher modal. - Bridge-based switches via URL parameters. - Cross-Domain Bridge links going through `/resolve` (server-side redirect). ## UI / UX fixes - Build sub-menu: fixed unreadable "Mapping" stale-indicator badge. - Build sub-menu: stopped reporting "Loaded" for the Graph DB digital twin when nothing had actually been built. - Sidebar: fixed the "Teams" icon misalignment. - Cockpit: the **Active Version** tile now reflects the version exposed via API/MCP (the one set in **Registry → Browse**), not merely the latest version on disk, with a `(not loaded)` hint when the loaded version differs. `is_active` keeps its legacy `is_latest` meaning so the read-only body class still gates writes correctly. - Navbar: the **Domain name and version** in the top navbar now refresh reliably after every domain mutation (new domain, load from registry, save / rename, version switch / create / rollback, file import). The `/navbar/state` `sessionStorage` cache (15 s TTL) was previously surviving `window.location.reload()`, so the navbar could display the *previous* domain identity for up to 15 s. Every mutation flow now invalidates the cache before navigating; in-place edits (e.g. saving Domain Information) re-fetch the navbar state immediately. - Domain → **Versions**: the API/MCP “Active” control is no longer a toggle on this page — it is shown as a **read-only badge**; changing the active version is done only from **Registry → Browse** (consistent with registry-centric operations). - Domain creation: **Save to UC is now blocked** when the chosen Domain Name already exists in the registry. The duplicate-name check (`/domain/check-name`) was already running on every keystroke of the name field, but its result was only advisory — the navbar's Save action still POSTed and the user only saw the conflict after a round-trip. The Save flow now re-runs the check synchronously and refuses with a clear notification + focuses the offending field. ## Documentation - **README**, **docs/features.md**, **docs/INFO.md**, **docs/user-guide.md**, **docs/get-started.md**, **docs/README.md**, and **docs/mcp.md** updated so operator-facing text matches the above: Ontology **Designer**, Domain Cockpit **Active Version** vs loaded vs latest, **Registry → Browse** for MCP/API active version, new-domain loading overlay, Digital Twin path refresh on committed name/version changes, duplicate-name guard, and navbar identity refresh. - **`docs/deployment.md`** rewritten for the current DAB: **`dev` / `dev-lakebase`** targets, correct **`bundle deployment bind`** / **`bundle run`** resource keys and app names, **`scripts/deploy.sh`** flags (no legacy `--all` / `--mcp-only`), **Lakebase** variable summary, **Step 5b** for **`bootstrap-lakebase-perms.sh`**, full deployment checklist, MCP and troubleshooting sections, and **§9 DAB reference** aligned with the **`Makefile`**. - **README** Lakebase paragraph: documents **`lakebase_database_resource_segment`** and the `list-databases` lookup pattern. ## Tasks & Notifications - Tasks panel now shows only currently running tasks; finished tasks are moved to the Notifications drawer. ## Backend & Databricks Apps bundle (operator-facing) - Lakebase **registry** backend wired end-to-end (runtime + optional Volume toggle unchanged). - **`databricks.yml`**: `ontobricks_dev_app` / `mcp_ontobricks_app` resource keys; workspace app names **`ontobricks-020`** and **`mcp-ontobricks`**; `dev-lakebase` target adds the Apps **`postgres`** resource whose `database` path ends with **`lakebase_database_resource_segment`** (`db-…` from the Postgres API `name` field). - **`scripts/deploy.sh`**: default target **`dev-lakebase`**; **`APP_NAME`** set to **`ontobricks-020`** so post-deploy **`bootstrap-app-permissions.sh`** and **`bootstrap-lakebase-perms.sh`** resolve the correct service principal. - **`scripts/bootstrap-lakebase-perms.sh`**: default Lakebase project **`ontobricks-app`**, default Postgres DB **`ontobricks_registry`** (dedicated `datname` aligned with the bundle bind), schema **`ontobricks_registry`**; default grantees **`ontobricks-020`** and **`mcp-ontobricks`**. Use **`-d databricks_postgres`** if the registry schema still lives in the shared default DB. Retarget with **`-i` / `-d` / `-s` / `-a`** when your workspace differs. - **`scripts/bootstrap-app-permissions.sh`**: default app list **`ontobricks-020`** **`mcp-ontobricks`** (matches the bundle). ## Security - Patched two GitPython advisories pulled in transitively via `mlflow-skinny`: - **GHSA-rpm5-65cw-6hj4** — command injection via `upload_pack` / `receive_pack` kwargs on `Repo.clone_from`, `Remote.fetch`, `Remote.pull`, `Remote.push` (affected `[3.1.30, 3.1.47)`). - **GHSA-x2qx-6953-8485 / CVE-2026-42284** — argument injection via `multi_options` `shlex.split` bypass in `_clone()` / `Submodule.update` (affected `<= 3.1.44`). - Both fixed by adding `gitpython>=3.1.47` to `[tool.uv].constraint-dependencies` in `pyproject.toml`; lockfile bumped `gitpython 3.1.46 → 3.1.47`. OntoBricks itself does not import `git` anywhere, so there is no code-path exposure — this only closes the SCA finding on the lockfile / installed env. --- ## Upgrade notes - **Databricks Apps sandbox name:** if you still point scripts or docs at **`ontobricks-dev`**, switch to **`ontobricks-020`** (the name in `databricks.yml` for `ontobricks_dev_app`) for `databricks apps get`, **`bootstrap-app-permissions.sh`**, and **`bootstrap-lakebase-perms.sh -a …`**, or pass **`-a`** explicitly. - **Lakebase bundle variables:** the monolithic branch/database path variables are replaced by **`lakebase_project`**, **`lakebase_branch`**, **`lakebase_database_resource_segment`** (must be the **`db-…`** segment from **`databricks postgres list-databases "projects//branches/" -o json`** — the Apps API does not accept the Postgres **`datname`** as the path tail), and **`lakebase_registry_schema`**. After each **`dev-lakebase`** deploy, re-run **`scripts/bootstrap-lakebase-perms.sh`** (or **`make bootstrap-lakebase`**) if the postgres resource was rebound, so the app SP keeps **USAGE** on the registry schema. - **`Makefile`:** **`make bootstrap-perms`** now passes **`ontobricks-020`** and **`mcp-ontobricks`**; **`make bootstrap-lakebase`** runs the Lakebase script with its built-in defaults (override with script flags when needed). - First-time deploys benefit from the SP-self-permission bootstrap; re-run **`make bootstrap-perms`** if the app name changed or bootstrap was skipped. - Viewer/Editor/Admin roles are now enforced in both the backend and the UI — verify your Teams matrix after upgrade if you rely on custom role assignments.
This discussion was created from the release v0.2.0.

nodes.title: Canonical design Part 1: Product architecture, workspace, review & i18n
nodes.body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Frozen — as of 2026-10-08, the authority for UIUX behavior and external contracts is the [`.spec/` directory](https://github.com/DevilTea/uiux/tree/main/.spec) in the repository** (Stories, Features and Rules, Contracts and Clauses, Scenarios; see [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/DevilTea/uiux/blob/main/AGENTS.md)). Where this Discussion and `.spec/` differ, `.spec/` wins.
>
> This Discussion keeps the rationale and history of the decisions it records. Its body and existing comments are not edited further. To propose a new or changed decision, add a new comment here or open a new Discussion; once the owner (@DevilTea) explicitly accepts it in that Discussion, a `.spec/` PR records it, and implementation PRs cite the spec unit IDs.

---

# Context

This document specifies **UIUX** (`@deviltea/uiux`), a local-first UI/UX specification, preview, and review workbench designed for human-agent collaboration.

## Canonical Discussion Map

- **Part 1 (this discussion):** product architecture, workspace, View/Variant/Review model, i18n/Checks, MCP, handoff, and top-level Preview/runtime architecture.
- **Part 2:** [Cross-iframe protocol core](https://github.com/DevilTea/uiux/discussions/2) — session/generation/capability handshake and recovery, reconnect/reload semantics, message schemas, cache/refinement state machines, and protocol diagnostics.
- **Part 3:** [Preview navigation, targeting & browser integration](https://github.com/DevilTea/uiux/discussions/3) — navigation, targeting interactions, observer lifecycle, overlay coordination, and browser mapping/measurement.
- **Part 4:** [Vector contours, occlusion & numerical conformance](https://github.com/DevilTea/uiux/discussions/4) — vector contour representation, geometric tolerance, occlusion/compositing, non-affine precision, and numerical conformance.
- **Part 5:** [i18n, Checks & translation runtime](https://github.com/DevilTea/uiux/discussions/5) — translation resources/runtime, Catalog i18n mapping, warning/evidence semantics, and Checks behavior.
- **Part 6:** [UX Flow & Prototype Architecture](https://github.com/DevilTea/uiux/discussions/6) — canonical Flow resources, steps/transitions, Widget Event triggers, deterministic prototype execution, Flow evidence, MCP, and Workbench graph/player behavior.
- **Part 7:** [Review Persistence & Thread Schema](https://github.com/DevilTea/uiux/discussions/7) — Review resource persistence, messages, actor/history provenance, submissions/evidence references, retention, MCP, and Workbench timeline behavior.
- **Part 8:** [Workspace Adapter Resolution & Configuration](https://github.com/DevilTea/uiux/discussions/8) — Workspace adapter selection/order, module resolution, adapter identity/API compatibility, config schemas, failure/install semantics, Handoff provenance, and Workbench Adapter/Catalog management.
- **Part 9:** [Authored Assets & Derived Artifact Storage](https://github.com/DevilTea/uiux/discussions/9) — authored asset identity/layout/bindings/replacement, validation, derived content-addressed artifact storage, and asset/artifact MCP boundaries.
- **Part 10:** [Render Context & Capture Semantics](https://github.com/DevilTea/uiux/discussions/10) — viewport/theme render-context identity, discovery, capture-context selection, and deterministic capture semantics.

Historical rationale remains preserved in earlier discussion comments. New decisions should be recorded in the canonical Part that owns their scope rather than duplicated across Parts.

Typical usage:

```sh
npm install -D @deviltea/uiux
npx uiux init --workspace ./design
npx uiux dev --workspace ./design
```

`uiux dev` runs a single local process combining:
- A Nuxt SPA (with Nuxt UI, `ssr: false`) for human browsing and review;
- An internal Nitro server hosting application HTTP endpoints (`/api/*`), agent MCP transport (`/mcp`), and preview/render services (`/preview/*`).

The SPA and MCP layer share the exact same underlying application domain services.

---

# Core Architecture & Foundations
**Accepted UIUX Adapter package entrypoint: one canonical adapter manifest export (option A).** A Design System Adapter package exposes one public adapter definition that declares its Widget plugin definitions, UIUX Catalog metadata, Vue renderer registrations, provider setup, and style/token resources. UIUX loads adapters through this contract rather than scanning package files or relying on component-by-component discovery.

**Accepted Widget/Catalog metadata boundary: Widget owns executable/schema truth; UIUX Adapter Catalog owns authoring metadata (option A).** Widget plugin definitions remain authoritative for runtime type/schema/defaults/Slots/Properties and other executable semantics. UIUX-specific labels/groups/icons, authoring controls, i18n field mappings, preview hints, and documentation metadata live in the Adapter Catalog and are not pushed into `@deviltea/widget-core` or duplicated as an independent runtime schema.

**Accepted adapter runtime loading: explicit manifest registration installed once per Preview runtime (option A).** Active adapters provide renderer registrations, provider setup, and global styles/tokens explicitly through the adapter manifest. UIUX installs them in declared order when constructing the Preview runtime. Filename conventions, filesystem/package scanning, and side-effect-only registration are not canonical loading mechanisms.

**Accepted shared/project adapter ownership: reusable Design System base adapter plus separate project extension adapters (option A).** The reusable base adapter evolves with the shared Design System and may be reused across Workspaces. Product-specific Widgets or Catalog metadata are layered through separate extension adapters selected explicitly by the Workspace rather than forking or mutating the base adapter at runtime.

**Accepted first-version public package topology: one public package (option A).** UIUX publishes a single npm package, `@deviltea/uiux`, containing the CLI, Nuxt/Nitro server, Workbench SPA, and internal domain services. Users install one public package rather than composing separate CLI/core/server packages.

**Accepted canonical npm package name: `@deviltea/uiux` (option A).** The documented install surface `npm install -D @deviltea/uiux` is canonical.

**Accepted canonical CLI binary name: `uiux` (option A).** The canonical command surface is `uiux`, including flows such as `npx uiux init` and `npx uiux dev`; the npm scope is not repeated in the executable name.

**Accepted first-version internal package boundary: one package with explicit source/module layering (option A).** CLI, server, Workbench, and domain responsibilities are separated through clear internal modules rather than premature private workspace packages. A package split is deferred until a concrete independent reuse or publication requirement exists.

## Widget as Executable View IR Runtime

UIUX builds upon [DevilTea/widget](https://github.com/DevilTea/widget) (`@deviltea/widget-core`, `@deviltea/widget-vue`) as its executable mockup runtime.
- **Responsibility boundary:** Widget owns executable view semantics, compilation, atomic patches, and inspection protocols. UIUX owns project organization, review, spec metadata, i18n, captures, handoff, and human/agent workflows.
- UIUX consumes Widget without pushing UIUX-specific concepts into `@deviltea/widget-core`.

## Design System Integration & Responsibility Split

**One shared Design System is the common foundation; UIUX and the production application consume it independently.**
- **Design System:** Owns production components, tokens, styles, and usage rules.
- **UIUX Adapter:** Wraps the Design System into authoring Widget plugins, Vue renderers, styles, and catalog metadata for design specifications.
- **UIUX Workspace:** Owns authored View IR, View Spec, named Variants, UX Flows, review threads, and handoff assets.
- **Production App:** Consumes UIUX handoff as technical/design reference, independently implementing application behavior, routing, and data layer.
- **Handoff is the boundary from UIUX to production**, not the Widget runtime or generated application code.

## Mockups as Executable Specifications

Mockups communicate view structure, component identity, states, copy, interaction rules, and visual reference. View IR must not expand into a secondary production application framework (no arbitrary business logic, networking, or routing).

---

# Location-Independent, File-Native Workspace
**Accepted Workspace manifest location: `.uiux/workspace.json` (option C).** The canonical Workspace manifest lives at `.uiux/workspace.json` under the selected Workspace root. It owns the already accepted manifest-level `schemaVersion` and Workspace-level settings; UIUX system metadata is therefore grouped under the reserved `.uiux/` directory rather than a root-level manifest filename.

**Accepted first-version View JSON top-level shape: `id`, `name`, optional `feature`, `ir`, `variants`, `spec` (option A).** `id` is the immutable full UUID, `name` is the required human-readable display name, `feature` is the optional single-valued virtual grouping tag, `ir` stores the canonical Widget tree, `variants` stores named Runtime State presets, and `spec` stores View Spec/decisions. Derived timestamps, source paths, filenames, or generic free-form `metadata` are not canonical top-level fields.

**Accepted RootShell primary Slot name: `content` (option A).** The persisted system RootShell exposes one required primary Slot named `content`, which contains the authored root-level Widget tree. The naming is framework-neutral and does not reuse Vue's `default` Slot name.

**Accepted first-version RootShell Slot cardinality: exactly one required `content` Slot containing 0..N ordered child Widgets (option A).** An empty View is represented by an empty ordered `content` child list. Authors cannot add arbitrary RootShell Slots in the first-version schema; introducing additional system Slots requires a schema migration.

**Accepted Workspace schema-version authority: one manifest-level `schemaVersion` (option A).** The Workspace manifest owns the single canonical integer schema version for the entire Workspace. Individual View JSON files do not duplicate independent schema versions; all files are decoded under the Workspace version. **The first product-owned Workspace schema version is `1`.** The initial recognized-version set is therefore `{1}` and the first version has no migration steps; future recognized older versions and deterministic migrations are additive product policy.

**Accepted Workspace migration policy: explicit deterministic in-place migration with write lockout beforehand (option A).** A recognized older Workspace may be inspected and explained, but UIUX must not silently mutate it. Mutating operations are blocked until the user explicitly invokes migration. Migration upgrades the Workspace atomically/deterministically to the target version; failure must not leave a partially migrated Workspace.

**Accepted RootShell canonical identity: system type `RootShell` with reserved ID `root` (option A).** Every View persists exactly one UIUX-managed root Widget with type `RootShell` and ID `root`. This identity is reserved and does not participate in ordinary author-defined/UUID Widget identity allocation.

**Accepted RootShell edit guard: structure and identity are system-managed; only explicitly user-editable fields may change (option A).** RootShell presence, type, ID, and required Slot structure are protected invariants. Authors may edit only RootShell props/config explicitly marked user-editable by schema; deleting/retyping/reidentifying the root or breaking required Slots is invalid even through raw file edits.

**Accepted: the CLI explicitly selects a self-contained UIUX Workspace root** (e.g. `uiux init --workspace ./design` and `uiux dev --workspace ./design`). UIUX owns the fixed internal file layout under that root in any repository or standalone directory, operating without requiring production source trees, Git, or network access.
**Accepted View-file unit: one View = one JSON file.** Widget IR, named Variant Runtime State presets, and View Spec cohabit separate logical sections within a single JSON file. Reviews, UX Flows, i18n resources, and assets remain separate workspace resources.
**Accepted workspace placement: all View JSON files live in a shared top-level `views/` directory, independently of Feature ownership.** All View JSON files reside in a flat top-level `views/` directory under the workspace root, independent of Feature ownership. Feature grouping in the Workbench is derived dynamically from each View's optional single-valued `feature` tag without moving files.
**Accepted View identity: each View has an immutable full UUID stored inside its JSON file, independent of its human-readable filename and display name.** Each View is identified by an immutable full UUID in its JSON `id` property, which serves as the canonical reference across UX Flows, Reviews, and Handoff. Moving or renaming the file does not alter identity, and shortened IDs or slug-based references are prohibited.
**Accepted filename convention: the filename is the entire UUID plus `.view.json`** Files must be named `<full-UUID>.view.json` matching the internal `id` property exactly, without slugs or abbreviations. The loader validates matching UUIDs, rejects duplicate IDs or filenames, and displays human-readable names from JSON metadata.
## Feature Display Grouping
Feature grouping is an optional View-local tag (`feature`) used solely for virtual categorization in Workbench navigation. There is no persisted Feature entity, directory hierarchy, or cross-resource Feature reference contract.

# Workflows, Reviews, & Decisions
**Accepted Review Widget anchor identity: stable `{ viewId, widgetId }` structural identity (option A).** A Widget-anchored Review thread is canonically bound to immutable View identity plus Widget identity. DOM selectors, rendered geometry, child indices, and tree paths are not part of anchor identity, so moving a Widget within the authored tree does not change the Review anchor.

**Accepted Review anchor fallback policy: no canonical selector/path fallback; non-authoritative display hints only (option A).** Workbench may retain historical labels, tree-path snapshots, or Preview snippets to help users understand a stale anchor, but resolution authority remains the stable IDs. Missing IDs must never auto-rebind to a different Widget through DOM selectors, tree positions, or geometry heuristics.

**Accepted deleted/unresolvable Review target behavior: preserve the thread and mark the anchor invalid; never auto-rebind (option A).** Review discussion remains canonical historical/design data even when its Widget disappears. Workbench surfaces a missing-target diagnostic and any available snapshot hint; a human may explicitly re-anchor or resolve the thread, but deletion does not silently close or redirect it.

**Accepted Review Variant scope: explicit `variantNames: string[]`, where `[]` means View-wide/all Variants (option A).** A Widget thread remains anchored to the same View/Widget while `variantNames` optionally narrows applicability to named Variant identities. An empty array means the thread is not Variant-specific and applies across current and future Variants. Missing named Variants become invalid sub-anchors without deleting the thread.

## Agent Workflow via MCP
The local server exposes domain-level MCP Resources/Tools across Workspace, Catalog, View, Preview, Review, Spec/i18n, UX Flow, authored Assets/derived Artifacts, and Handoff. Exact operations follow the accepted domain-specific Resource/Tool, mutation, pagination, and `expectedRevision` contracts in Parts 1 and 6–9; stale Project/Feature-registry assumptions are not part of the canonical API. Agents inspect canonical resources, author through domain mutations, validate/render/capture, manage Reviews, and export Handoff through the same shared application/domain services used by Workbench.

## Review Lifecycle & Evidence Gate
**Accepted ready-for-review change/evidence model: structured evidence bundle classified by change domain (option A).** Each Review submission records explicit change domains such as IR, Variant, Spec, i18n, or adapter/config changes and links the evidence that validates those changes. Workbench uses this machine-readable classification to determine which expensive evidence must be regenerated rather than inferring scope from prose alone.

**Accepted interaction verification: replayable structured interaction scripts executed with Playwright evidence (option A).** Interaction evidence is represented as structured steps, targets, and assertions that UIUX can replay against Preview. Execution records pass/fail outcomes and any required captures; arbitrary browser-session recordings, screenshots alone, or manual checklists are not the canonical verification mechanism.

**Accepted formal Review validation scope: whole canonical View + all named Variants, with change-scoped evidence reruns (option A).** A View may enter `ready-for-review` only when the entire canonical IR/spec is valid and every named Variant is executable. Expensive captures or interaction evidence may be selectively rerun based on structured change domains when unaffected prior evidence remains demonstrably valid; readiness never ignores invalid unchanged regions.

**Accepted Review/handoff screenshot retention: content-addressed immutable artifacts referenced by evidence records (option A).** Playwright capture bytes are stored by content identity and never overwritten in place. Review submissions and handoff evidence store artifact references plus capture context; identical bytes may deduplicate, while resolved Reviews retain access to the exact evidence captured at submission time.

Reviews follow a three-state lifecycle: `open` -> `ready-for-review` -> `resolved`. Humans hold exclusive resolution authority; agents submit revisions to `ready-for-review` accompanied by validation evidence (Playwright captures, diagnostics). Reviewers may resolve threads or return them to `open` with feedback.
**Accepted Review-to-Decision relationship: explicit promotion only.** Review comments do not automatically become View Spec decisions; promoting review feedback into a formal `spec.decisions` entry requires an explicit authoring action by a human or agent. Promoted decisions initialize in `pending` (unless settled), retain provenance links to source review threads, and maintain independent lifecycles.
## View Variant Realization
**Accepted Variant serialization: `variants` object keyed by Variant name, each entry containing `{ state }` (option A).** The canonical shape remains `variants.<name>.state.<widgetId>.<prop>`. Variants do not carry separate UUIDs or duplicate their name inside the entry; the entry object remains extensible for future additive metadata.

**Accepted Variant state storage: sparse overrides only (option A).** A Variant stores only state members it explicitly overrides relative to the canonical Widget IR/plugin defaults. Unspecified Widgets/properties inherit canonical defaults rather than being copied into a full Runtime State snapshot.

**Accepted Variant identity/discoverability: the Variant name is the View-local stable identity and is enumerated directly from `variants` keys (option A).** Variant names are non-empty and unique within a View. UX Flows, Reviews, and Handoff identify a Variant through `<viewId> + variantName`; renaming is an explicit identity change that requires reference updates, with no hidden Variant registry or secondary ID.

**Accepted invalid-Variant handling: preserve authored data, block execution, and report all determinable diagnostics (option A).** UIUX does not silently drop invalid overrides or partially apply a Variant containing invalid Widget IDs, state properties, or values. The authored Variant remains editable for repair, but cannot be used for render/capture/formal Review evidence until valid; inline context and Checks surface all determinable validation errors together.

A View defines one canonical Widget IR document with the persisted UIUX-owned RootShell as its root node. Named Variants represent initial Widget Runtime State presets (`variants.<name>.state.<widgetId>.<prop>`) applied via Widget Core's `createRuntime({ overrideStateDefaults })`. UIUX treats invalid Widget IDs, unknown state members, and invalid values as validation errors rather than silently accepting partial presets.

# View IR vs View Spec
**Accepted decision transition graph: `pending`↔`deferred`, `pending`/`deferred`→`decided`, and explicit `decided`→`pending` reopen (option A).** Status changes occur only through explicit lifecycle actions. A decided decision may be reopened when assumptions or requirements change; reopening returns it to `pending` rather than silently editing a terminal record. On `decided`→`pending` reopen, the current `outcome` is cleared; the previously decided outcome remains preserved only through append-only `history[]` before/after semantics.

**Accepted decision lifecycle history: append-only structured `history[]` in canonical View JSON (option A).** Each decision retains current `status`/`outcome` plus append-only lifecycle events recording status/outcome mutations with time, actor/source, and before/after semantics. Repository history remains useful, but understanding a decision lifecycle does not depend on Git/file history.

**Accepted Review-to-Decision promotion idempotency: provenance-keyed reuse (option A).** A promoted decision records the source Review thread identity. Repeating the promote action for the same source returns/navigates the existing decision instead of creating a duplicate. Creating an additional independent decision from the same Review source requires a distinct explicit action.

**Accepted View-to-View reference shape: typed `{ type: "view", viewId, variantName?, relation? }` (option A).** `viewId` is required; `variantName` optionally targets a named Variant; `relation` optionally records a non-empty design-semantic relationship. View Spec references do not become UX Flow edges or runtime routing. The `references` array remains extensible as a typed union for other reference categories.

**Accepted View Spec core shape: prose `intent`, ordered string-list categories, structured `references`, and structured `decisions` (option A).** The canonical first-version `spec` fields are `intent: string`, `entryConditions: string[]`, `interactionRules: string[]`, `constraints: string[]`, `accessibility: string[]`, `references: Reference[]`, and `decisions: Decision[]`. The prose/list categories do not introduce per-item IDs in the first-version schema.

**Accepted View Spec field presence: all canonical fields are required and represent empty content explicitly (option A).** `spec` always exists. `intent` is always a string and may be empty; every list field always exists and may be `[]`. Schema shape is deterministic and does not use field omission to encode authoring completeness; Checks/Review policy evaluates content completeness separately.

**Accepted Spec decision identity: immutable full UUID (option A).** Each `spec.decisions[]` item receives a full UUID on creation. Decisions remain stored View-locally but their IDs are globally unique so references, provenance, handoff, and any future cross-View movement do not depend on array index, title text, or a View-local sequence.

**Accepted decided-outcome schema: structured `{ summary, rationale }` (option A).** When a decision reaches `decided`, `outcome.summary` is a required non-empty settled result and `outcome.rationale` is a required string that may be empty. The original decision prompt/question and provenance remain separate canonical fields rather than being overwritten by the outcome.

**Accepted: View IR and View Spec remain conceptually distinct, but live in named sections of the same View JSON file alongside Variants.** View IR defines executable rendering structure, while View Spec captures design purpose, constraints, and decisions.
**Accepted View Spec direction: a structured UI/UX specification, including open decisions.** The View-local `spec` section captures structured design semantics across standardized categories: intent, entry conditions, interaction rules, constraints, accessibility, external references, accepted decisions, and open decisions. Outstanding open decisions retain stable local identities and are indexed into a global Workbench inbox for cross-View discovery and direct target navigation.
**Accepted decision lifecycle: pending / decided / deferred.** Spec decisions transition through three explicit states: `pending` (active in the Workbench inbox), `decided` (resolved with recorded outcome and rationale, removed from inbox), and `deferred` (shelved and discoverable without cluttering the primary queue, capable of being reopened). Deferral does not imply approval, and decision status remains decoupled from Review thread lifecycle.
**Accepted storage: one unified `spec.decisions` array for every decision regardless of its current state.** All View decisions are stored in a single unified `spec.decisions` array on each View JSON, where each item maintains a stable identifier and updates its `status` property in place. Decided items record structured outcomes and rationales, while Workbench derives filtered pending/deferred/decided queues directly from these canonical arrays.

# Downstream Contracts & Infrastructure

## Handoff
Handoff serves as the authoritative boundary from UIUX to production. It exports implementation-friendly structured reference data:
- Canonical `i18n/<locale>.json` message files (with empty and whitespace strings preserved verbatim);
- Shared design-system component references and token bindings;
- View Specs (intent, entry conditions, constraints, accessibility);
- UX Flow transition maps;
- Deterministic screenshot captures.

**Accepted source-backed implementation-reference principle:** for every used Widget type, Handoff must make the Widget plugin semantic source and renderer/source integration traceable, and where relevant expose the referenced Design System component public API/docs/source plus narrow supporting code. These materials are curated implementation evidence, not production code generation or an instruction to copy UIUX wrappers verbatim. Materialization follows the accepted curated content-addressed snapshot + pinned-provenance model in the Handoff decision index below.

## Screenshot & Capture
UIUX integrates a Playwright-based capture engine for automated screenshot generation across viewports, locales, and named Variants. Captures serve as immutable visual evidence for Review transitions and handoff assets.

## CLI & Server
The CLI package `@deviltea/uiux` provides:
- `uiux init --workspace <dir>`: Initializing a valid workspace skeleton.
- `uiux dev --workspace <dir>`: Starting the unified Nuxt/Nitro server hosting SPA, API, MCP, and preview endpoints.

## Current Non-Goals
- UIUX is not a production application framework (no arbitrary business logic or server deployment generation).
- UIUX is not a general project-management or issue-tracking tool.
- UIUX is not a multi-tenant cloud SaaS; it is strictly local-first and file-native.

# Canonical Decision Index

The following 12 areas summarize the original first-version decision domains and their current canonical status:

1. **Package/repo naming and package boundaries**
   - Accepted: one public package `@deviltea/uiux`, CLI binary `uiux`, and one-package internal module layering for the first version.
   - No remaining first-version open decision in this area; future package extraction requires a concrete independent reuse/publication need.

2. **Workspace schema**
   - Accepted: Workspace root; `.uiux/workspace.json` manifest; one-View/one-JSON-file; flat `views/` directory; full UUID identity/filename; View top-level fields `id`, `name`, optional `feature`, `ir`, `variants`, `spec`; manifest-level single `schemaVersion` with first product version `1`; explicit atomic in-place migration; RootShell type `RootShell` + reserved ID `root`; exactly one required `content` Slot containing 0..N ordered child Widgets; and system-managed root structure/identity with schema-limited user-editable fields.
   - No remaining first-version structural Workspace/View schema decision in this area. Workspace settings payloads that belong to i18n/Checks remain tracked under item 8.

3. **Widget integration contract**
   - Accepted: RootShell persisted as canonical root Widget plugin; one adapter-manifest public entrypoint; Widget plugin definitions own executable/schema truth; UIUX Adapter Catalog owns authoring metadata; renderer/provider/style resources are explicitly registered through the manifest and installed once per Preview runtime; shared Design System base adapters are extended by separately selected project extension adapters.
   - No remaining first-version open decision in this area.

4. **View Variant schema and validation**
   - Accepted: named Variant Runtime State presets serialized as a `variants` object keyed by View-local stable Variant name; each entry contains sparse `{ state }` overrides; names are discovered directly from keys and referenced as `<viewId> + variantName`; invalid authored Variants are preserved but non-executable and report all determinable diagnostics without partial apply.
   - No remaining first-version open decision in this area.

5. **View Spec schema**
   - Accepted: canonical fields `intent`, `entryConditions`, `interactionRules`, `constraints`, `accessibility`, structured `references`, and structured `decisions`; all fields always present with explicit empty values; decision inbox; lifecycle `pending`↔`deferred`, `pending`/`deferred`→`decided`, explicit `decided`→`pending` reopen with current `outcome` cleared and prior outcome retained in `history[]`; unified `spec.decisions` array; immutable full-UUID decision IDs; decided outcomes `{ summary, rationale }`; append-only structured decision history; provenance-idempotent Review promotion; typed View references `{ type: "view", viewId, variantName?, relation? }`; and provider-agnostic external references `{ type: "external", uri, label?, relation? }`.
   - External `uri` is a required non-empty absolute URI. It may use `https:` or any other valid absolute-URI scheme such as `urn:`; UIUX does not define provider-specific `source/id` semantics in the first-version Reference union.
   - Optional `label` is non-authoritative display text/cache only. Optional `relation` records a non-empty design-semantic relationship. Neither field changes external identity.
   - UIUX does not automatically fetch, mirror, synchronize, or domain-validate external-reference content, and failure to resolve/reach the URI does not rewrite the canonical View Spec reference.
   - No remaining first-version View Spec schema decision is currently listed after convergence audit.

6. **Review anchor model**
   - Accepted: Widget anchors use stable `{ viewId, widgetId }`; selector/path/geometry data may exist only as non-authoritative display hints; missing/deleted targets preserve the thread with an invalid-anchor diagnostic and require explicit re-anchor; Variant scope is `variantNames: string[]`, with `[]` meaning View-wide/all Variants.
   - No remaining first-version open decision in this area.

7. **Review lifecycle**
   - Accepted: Three-state model (`open`, `ready-for-review`, `resolved`) with human-only resolution authority; structured evidence bundles classified by change domain; replayable structured interaction verification executed through Playwright; readiness validation covers the whole canonical View and all named Variants while expensive evidence may be minimally rerun by change domain; Review/handoff screenshots are content-addressed immutable artifacts referenced by evidence records; Review-to-Decision promotion idempotency is defined under item 5.
   - No remaining first-version open decision in this area.

8. **i18n schema, Checks, and translation runtime behavior**
   - Canonical detailed design: [Discussion #5](https://github.com/DevilTea/uiux/discussions/5).
   - Accepted product-level direction: UIUX-owned canonical translations, flat locale resources, explicit primary locale, RootShell `t`, Adapter Catalog mapping, normalized Checks, structured warnings/evidence, and warning-only Review readiness.
   - Detailed i18n/Checks decisions are canonical in Part 5; Part 5 currently lists no remaining first-version open questions.

9. **MCP API**
   - Accepted first-version boundary:
     - **Resources** provide stable-URI point reads for directly addressable canonical read models such as Workspace, an individual View/Spec, locale resources, and immutable artifacts.
     - **Ratified Resource-URI scope consequence:** first-version Resource URIs are required to be stable within the namespace of the running server's explicitly selected Workspace. UIUX does not add a persistent Workspace UUID solely to globalize MCP Resource URIs. Resource addressing combines resource kind with the resource's canonical identity/key within that selected Workspace; the exact URI grammar is a protocol implementation detail to freeze when the MCP surface is implemented. MCP Resource URIs are not portable/global Handoff identities: exported bundles use their manifest, canonical resource identities/revisions, and content digests for portable provenance.
     - Discovery/filter/search/list/pagination remain read-only **Tools**; all mutations and imperative actions such as validate/render/capture/Review actions are Tools. The same mutation is not exposed through a parallel resource-write contract.
     - Mutations are **domain-specific and atomic**. A mutation may carry multiple structured operations against the same canonical resource/domain boundary (for example `patch_view`, `patch_view_spec`, `patch_messages`, or a Review action), but the first version does not expose generic `write_file`, arbitrary filesystem writes, or cross-domain Workspace-wide JSON Patch transactions.
     - Every mutable canonical resource exposes an **opaque content-derived revision**. Read/query results include the current revision, callers must not infer semantics from its representation, and every mutation requires `expectedRevision`. A mismatch performs no write and returns a structured conflict including `currentRevision`; a successful mutation returns the new revision. This remains valid across process restarts and detects out-of-band edits.
     - Responses are **compact structured by default**. List/search results return identity, essential summary, and revision, with explicit cursor/limit pagination and detail/fields expansion. Large bodies/artifacts are referenced by stable Resource URI/ref instead of duplicated into tool results. Mutation responses default to affected identity, new revision, diagnostics, and change summary rather than the entire Workspace.
     - **Accepted destructive referential-integrity policy:** View, UX Flow, authored Asset, and identity-changing Variant operations may proceed as target-local mutations even when they invalidate references held by other canonical resources, but only after reference-impact analysis is returned and the caller explicitly acknowledges the known impact.
     - The destructive mutation changes only the target resource/domain boundary; UIUX does not auto-cascade, auto-rebind, or silently rewrite other canonical resources.
     - Existing external references preserve their original target identity and become structured invalid/dangling diagnostics until explicitly repaired. This is a supported repairable Workspace state, consistent with the existing invalid-authored-data preservation rules.
     - Out-of-band filesystem edits remain detectable through the same validation/reference analysis, but do not receive the UI/MCP acknowledgement affordance because they bypass normal mutation APIs.

10. **Preview/runtime architecture inside the accepted Nuxt/Nitro stack**
    - Canonical detailed protocol/integration split: [Part 2 protocol core](https://github.com/DevilTea/uiux/discussions/2), [Part 3 Preview integration](https://github.com/DevilTea/uiux/discussions/3), and [Part 4 vector/occlusion](https://github.com/DevilTea/uiux/discussions/4).
    - Accepted top-level runtime/module boundary:
      - UIUX reuses only **generalizable low-level Widget devtools primitives** where their semantics match—such as Inspector Agent capabilities, transport, frame bootstrap, and projection helpers. UIUX does not depend on Widget Lab application modules, and the current private experimental `@deviltea/widget-devtools` wire protocol is not elevated into the canonical UIUX Preview protocol. Parts 2–4 remain authoritative; any reuse is behind a UIUX-owned bridge/adapter.
      - `/preview/*` may be hosted same-origin with Workbench, but the Preview iframe is still a **strict document/runtime isolation boundary** in product semantics. Workbench does not directly reach into iframe DOM, Widget Runtime, or Blueprint objects for normal control/inspection. Normal control flows through the accepted cross-iframe protocol/dedicated channel. Playwright may inspect/capture from browser automation for evidence, but is not a Workbench control path.
      - The iframe owns a **UIUX Preview runtime bridge** that wraps any reused inspector primitives and exposes only UIUX canonical IDs/DTOs/protocol. DOM-aware hit testing, Runtime/Widget identity resolution, and inner geometry stay iframe/runtime responsibilities per Parts 2–4; Workbench receives only the canonical structural/geometry data and never raw DOM/Runtime/Blueprint objects.
      - Nitro exposes `/api/*`, `/mcp`, and `/preview/*` as separate **transport/hosting adapters** over one shared internal application/domain-service layer. `/api/*` serves Workbench HTTP operations; `/mcp` serves agent MCP transport; `/preview/*` serves Preview document/bootstrap/runtime assets and required hosting. MCP does not loop back through `/api/*`, and transport routes do not duplicate domain business logic.
    - No remaining first-version open decision in this area.

11. **Export/handoff contract**
    - Accepted first-version handoff boundary:
      - **Canonical authored resources remain canonical in their existing source formats** and are included/referenced directly by the handoff. The export does not invent a second equivalent View/Spec/i18n schema. Derived screenshots, rendered previews, Checks/evidence outputs, and similar products are explicitly represented as derived artifacts with typed refs/hashes/context in the handoff manifest.
      - Each export is an **immutable content-addressed bundle with a root manifest**. The manifest records its schema version, export identity/time, selected scope, canonical resource refs/snapshots, derived artifact refs, evidence refs, and provenance. Exporting again creates a new bundle identity; unchanged content-addressed artifacts may be reused/deduplicated rather than overwritten in place.
      - Provenance is sufficient to reproduce and interpret each exported item: Workspace schema version and export scope; canonical resource identity/revision; applicable View/Variant/locale/viewport and other capture/evidence context; producing UIUX/tool/engine version; and required evidence refs. Git commit identity may be included when available but is not required for canonical provenance, and provenance fields are not pushed back into canonical View schemas.
      - Implementation agents consume handoff through a **manifest-first, read-only reference contract**. They read the root manifest, follow canonical resource and derived-evidence refs as needed, and independently implement production code. The UIUX Widget runtime, RootShell, Adapter runtime plumbing, Preview runtime, and other UIUX execution internals are not production implementation contracts, and implementation agents do not write back into immutable handoff bundles.
      - Existing accepted screenshot policy remains in force: Playwright is the capture engine and formal Review/handoff screenshots are content-addressed immutable artifacts. Existing Part 5 handoff policy also remains in force: canonical `i18n/<locale>.json` resources and authored `$i18n` bindings/parameter-binding provenance are exported, while UIUX translation-runtime plumbing remains internal.
    - **Accepted Handoff selected-scope semantics:** an export starts from explicit typed resource roots and computes a deterministic transitive dependency closure. Roots may include the whole Workspace, selected Views, selected UX Flows, or other explicitly supported canonical resource types. The closure includes every canonical/derived dependency required to interpret and implement those roots, such as Flow target Views/Variants, referenced authored assets, applicable locale resources, adapter/source provenance, and selected formal evidence. Whole-Workspace export is a convenience preset, not the only model. The View-local `feature` tag is never elevated into an ownership boundary or canonical export entity.
    - **Accepted source-backed implementation-reference materialization:** Handoff uses a curated hybrid model. Adapter-provided mappings identify the Widget plugin semantic source, renderer/source integration, and where relevant the referenced Design System API/docs/source plus narrow supporting files for Widget types actually used by the selected scope. Materializable files are snapshotted into the immutable bundle by content identity while preserving pinned original package/repository/revision/path provenance. Sources that cannot or must not be materialized are explicitly marked provenance-only or unavailable rather than silently omitted. These references remain implementation evidence, not generated production code or an instruction to copy UIUX wrappers verbatim.
    - **Accepted export/readiness split:** a Handoff bundle may still be exported when the selected scope is incomplete, invalid, insufficiently evidenced, or not fully reviewed, provided the canonical scope is readable enough to produce a coherent immutable snapshot. The root manifest must expose machine-readable validation/evidence/review coverage and blocking diagnostics. Only a bundle satisfying the formal readiness gate may assert an `implementation-ready` status/claim; other bundles remain valid diagnostic/incremental handoff snapshots and must not imply readiness.
    - **Ratified readiness-closure consequence:** `implementation-ready` is evaluated only over the export's explicit roots and their deterministic dependency closure. Invalid Views, open Reviews, unused assets, or other incomplete Workspace resources outside that closure do not make the bundle non-ready. Conversely, any blocking invalid dependency or required missing evidence inside the closure prevents the readiness claim.
    - No remaining first-version Handoff architecture decision is currently listed after convergence audit.

12. **Collaboration beyond one workstation**
    - Accepted evolution boundary:
      - The first version is formally **single-user, local-first**. CLI/Nitro/Workbench/MCP are supported on one workstation for one user; the data and transport boundaries should remain extensible to future shared/hosted operation without pretending that multi-user consistency already exists.
      - Loopback-only local mode may remain **unauthenticated for low friction**. Any future bind/exposure beyond loopback—LAN or hosted—requires explicit authentication and authorization. Workbench HTTP/API, MCP, and Preview/session-sensitive endpoints share an authenticated principal/authorization policy rather than treating a private network as sufficient trust.
      - Future shared/hosted write concurrency extends the already accepted **per-resource opaque revision + required `expectedRevision`** contract. Competing writes return structured conflicts and require explicit reread/retry/rework; the architecture does not promise implicit merge, CRDT, or OT semantics.
      - Presence and live collaboration notifications are **ephemeral channels**, not canonical Workspace state. Future SSE/WebSocket/other push may carry active View, selection, typing/presence, and resource-changed notifications, but canonical state still changes only through normal validated mutations/revisions; reconnect resynchronizes from canonical resources.
    - No remaining first-version open decision in this area.

# Architecture Convergence Closure

As of the completed first-version convergence audit, **Parts 1–10 contain no known remaining first-version architecture-open decisions**. This is a closure of the architecture/protocol decision phase, not authorization to implement. If implementation planning exposes a contradiction or requires inventing a new persisted/external semantic contract, that item must return to architecture review instead of being silently decided in code.

## Implementation-entry checklist — non-normative execution order

The following is an implementation-entry checklist derived from the accepted architecture. It organizes work but does not create new canonical product semantics:

1. **Extract machine-checkable schemas and DTOs from the canonical records.** Freeze Workspace/View/Spec/Variant, Flow, Review, Adapter manifest/config, authored Asset, render-context, evidence, and Handoff data shapes. Any ambiguity that would change persisted/external meaning is an architecture regression and must be surfaced rather than guessed.
2. **Freeze domain service boundaries before transport/UI wiring.** Implement one shared application/domain layer for canonical reads, validation, domain-specific mutations, optimistic `expectedRevision`, reference-impact analysis, and diagnostics; `/api/*`, `/mcp`, Workbench, and Preview adapters must not fork business semantics.
3. **Implement file-native persistence and deterministic identity/revision behavior.** Cover `.uiux/workspace.json`, `views/`, `flows/`, `reviews/`, `i18n/`, `assets/`, and immutable `.uiux/artifacts/sha256/`, including out-of-band edit detection and explicit Workspace migration rules.
4. **Implement Adapter resolution/Catalog/runtime installation as one validated set.** Preserve explicit `adapters[]` ordering, portable module resolution, adapter API/config validation, collision rejection, and repairable invalid-Workspace behavior before authoritative Preview/Catalog construction.
5. **Implement the Preview bridge/protocol exactly from Parts 2–4.** Keep iframe/runtime ownership, Workbench overlay ownership, targeting/geometry/vector precision, cancellation, clipping/occlusion, and stale-response behavior behind the UIUX-owned protocol boundary.
6. **Implement render-context and deterministic capture/evidence.** Use Workspace-local viewport/theme keys, explicit resolved capture contexts, fresh formal-capture Runtime initialization, Playwright execution, deterministic structured evidence, and immutable `sha256:<hex>` evidence/artifact identities.
7. **Implement Review and decision workflows on top of immutable evidence.** Preserve append-only messages/history/submissions, `{ kind, evidence }` refs, human-only resolution, explicit Review-to-Decision promotion, and stale-anchor repair semantics.
8. **Implement UX Flow authoring/playback from the one canonical keyed/nested graph model.** Do not create a second graph schema or transition UUID model; replay recipes remain evidence-owned.
9. **Implement Handoff last as a manifest-first immutable export over already-working canonical resources/evidence.** Use explicit roots + deterministic dependency closure, source-backed implementation-reference snapshots/provenance, machine-readable readiness/coverage, and closure-scoped `implementation-ready` evaluation.
10. **Gate completion on conformance and adversarial tests, not coverage percentage.** Tests must distinguish valid/invalid states, stale revisions, dangling references, adapter failures, protocol ordering/cancellation, geometry tolerances, incomplete evidence coverage, and reproducible Handoff consumption.

## Authorization boundary

This closure does **not** authorize production implementation, Issues, PRs, merges, releases, or repository code changes. Those begin only after explicit user authorization.

---

# Design Principle to Preserve

> **Workspace files own the specification; Git versions them when present. Widget executes the view model. The browser is the human review surface. MCP is the agent authoring surface. Production code remains a separate implementation.**
